name: Resection Planning and Margins
title: Resection Planning and Margins
answer: This page covers AI systems that help surgical teams plan tissue resection and define safe margins before and during an operation. It includes tools for tumor boundary detection, organ sparing, and margin status prediction across oncology and other resection based procedures. The focus is on how computational models turn imaging and patient data into a surgical plan that a surgeon can review and adjust. It sits within surgical robotics and navigation because the output often feeds directly into robotic or navigated instruments.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: This page covers AI systems that help surgical teams plan tissue resection and define safe margins before and during an operation. It includes tools for tumor boundary detection, organ sparing, and margin status prediction across oncology and other resection based procedures. The focus is on how computational models turn imaging and patient data into a surgical plan that a surgeon can review and adjust. It sits within surgical robotics and navigation because the output often feeds directly into robotic or navigated instruments.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These tools generally run on preoperative imaging workstations and surgical navigation platforms, using CT, MRI, or PET scans as the main input. Many require GPU enabled local servers or cloud compute for segmentation and 3D model building, with a lower latency path for intraoperative updates. Robotic systems and optical or electromagnetic trackers provide the real time position data that aligns the plan to the patient on the table. The infrastructure usually includes a secure link between the planning software and the operating room display.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work begins with automated or semi automated segmentation of the target lesion and surrounding critical structures from volumetric scans. Machine learning models, often convolutional networks trained on annotated cases, then estimate the tumor extent and propose a resection volume with a defined margin. Deformable registration maps that plan onto the live patient, and some systems update the margin as tissue shifts or as new intraoperative imaging arrives. A surgeon reviews and modifies the proposed plan before any cut is made.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Training data provenance and patient consent are central, because models learn from real surgical cases and imaging that may carry identifying detail. Regulatory clearance usually requires evidence that the tool does not increase the rate of positive margins or harm critical structures, and validation must cover the populations and imaging protocols where it will be used. The site currently tracks six active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, a reminder that margin errors can become legal claims. Responsibility for the final resection decision remains with the surgeon, but the vendor may share liability if the tool's output is defective.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward real time intraoperative margin assessment, where optical or molecular signals are fused with the preoperative plan to tell the surgeon whether the margin is clear before closing. Augmented reality overlays and robotic autonomy are likely to make the planned resection volume more directly executable, with the robot constrained to the approved margin. Personalized margin models that weigh tumor biology against functional risk are also emerging. Over time these tools may shift from static preoperative plans to continuously updated guidance during the operation.
